prerequisites: Concepts of energy systems and turbo machinery with particular reference to gas-turbine cycles and multistage gas turbines.
Concepts of convective and radiation heat exchange.
Concepts of numerical calculation and experimental techniques

learning_outcomes.text: To be able to evaluate the performance of an aero-gas turbine propulsion system under real operating conditions.
To understand and compare different types of propulsion systems, with particular attention to combustion systems, the fuels used and their environmental impact.
Understand and compare the various control systems for gas turbine propulsion systems.
Be able to model and simulate the actual operation of an aeroengine using appropriate software, based on simple datasheets or publicly available repositories.
To be able to develop, test and evaluate own judgement capabilities through the preparation of a project relating to the simulation of a specific propulsion system and the oral examination.
To be able to develop, test and evaluate own communication skills through the preparation of a project relating to the simulation of a specific propulsion system and the oral examination.
To be able to develop, test and evaluate own learning skills through the preparation of a project relating to the simulation of a specific propulsion system and the oral examination.
Be able to evaluate the performance of a gas turbine-based power plant under real operating conditions.
Understand and compare different types of power plants, with particular attention to combustion systems, the fuels used and their environmental impact.
Understand and compare the various control systems used in gas turbine plants.
Be able to model and simulate the actual operation of a gas turbine plant using appropriate software, based on simple, available datasheets.
To be able to develop, test and evaluate own judgement capability through the preparation of a specific report on the simulation of a particular plant, and the oral examination.
To be able to develop, test and evaluate own communication skills through the preparation of a specific report on the simulation of a particular plant, and the oral examination.
To be able to develop, test and evaluate own learning skills through the preparation of a specific report on the simulation of a particular plant, and the oral examination.

syllabus_topics: Development Trend of gas turbine aeroengines
Operability and civil flight missions analysis
Gas turbine powerplants -Actual development trend and application
Gas turbine and combined cycle off-design analysis
Energy systems simulations approach and training lab
Ambient temperature and pressure effects on the engine performance
Partial load operability and control systems
Gas turbine powerplants and industrial applications
Gas turbine and combined cycle off-design analysis
Protection systems (Film cooling and Barrier coatings)
Secondary air system and sealing solutions
teaching_methods: Workshops with activities in small groups
Guided tours to industries and laboratories

assessment_methods.method: Thermo-fluidodynamic Analysis Laboratory (numerical, experimental and design-oriented) of high-temperature machine components (Part B)

assessment_rules: The overall assessment includes both the AeroEngine Modelling Laboratory (or Gas Turbine Modelling Laboratory for Part A) and an oral examination. The oral examination discusses the project from the laboratory. Attendance at prescribed laboratory sessions (Parts B and C) is verified. If laboratory attendance is partial or unverified, specific skills will be assessed through further questions in the oral examination. Grades range from Fail (Insufficient) to 29-30 and Honors (Lode) for excellent performance.
